title: Secatogue Neck
summary: Secatogue is recorded as a neck of land in Islip and the locality associated with the Secatogue people.
history_content: The name appears in Dutch and English records by the mid-seventeenth century, including records of meadow rights and references to the Black Grass Meadows.
translation_content:
Secatogue is interpreted as "black or dark colored land," connected to dark meadowland.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names reflect not only the uniqueness of a community’s cultural heritage but also serve as a tie to the rich history of the place.”

— Jeannet Stephen, Jabil Mapjabil, Nor Arifah Mohd Nor, and Patricia Antoinette P., Indigenous Place Names’ Continued Existence as Markers of Indigenous Identity in Sabah (2021), Abstract, opening sentence

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
preservation_content: Secatogue Neck connects a Native community name with a specific south-shore meadow landscape in Islip. It belongs alongside separate records for Secatogue people and territory.
